semantic_correction.stem: A nursing unit tests a new bedside handoff checklist for 1 week. After the test is completed, the RN joins the quality-improvement team for the Study phase of the Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle. Which action should the team take during this phase?

options.A: Review the selected metrics, assess how well the plan worked, and identify problems or potential solutions.
options.B: Define the improvement goal, select success metrics, and draft the plan for testing the checklist.
options.C: Implement the checklist on the selected unit and document what occurs during the test.
options.D: Use the lessons from the test to decide how the checklist or the next improvement cycle should be adapted.

semantic_correction.rationale: AHRQ describes the Study phase of the PDSA cycle as reviewing and monitoring the selected metrics, assessing how well the plan works, and identifying problems and potential solutions. Option A therefore matches the Study phase. Option B describes Plan, option C describes Do, and option D describes Act, in which lessons from the cycle are integrated to determine adaptations and next steps.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Differentiate the Study phase of a PDSA quality-improvement cycle from the Plan, Do, and Act phases by identifying its focus on reviewing metrics and analyzing test results.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
semantic_correction.source_locator: The cycle has four main parts — Study
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: In PDSA, Study involves reviewing and monitoring selected metrics, assessing how well the plan works, and identifying problems and potential solutions; Plan defines goals/metrics/action plan, Do implements the test, and Act integrates lessons to adapt next steps.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p. 7 / PDF p. 11, Related Activity Statements — Participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes
semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality improvement processes
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: replaced the original organizational Transition-to-Practice outcome-research item with an entry-level RN quality-improvement construct directly mapped to the 2026 Management of Care activity statement; rebuilt all four options from authoritative AHRQ PDSA phases.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original item asked about outcome measures used in an NCSBN transition-to-practice research study, which was not sufficiently aligned to an entry-level RN Management of Care activity. The item was rebuilt around direct participation in a PDSA quality-improvement process.
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p. 7 — Participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes

option_audit.A: Correct. This is AHRQ's Study phase: review/monitor metrics, assess performance, and identify problems or potential solutions.
option_audit.B: Plausible and source-supported PDSA activity, but it belongs to Plan rather than Study.
option_audit.C: Plausible and source-supported PDSA activity, but implementing the planned test belongs to Do.
option_audit.D: Plausible and source-supported PDSA activity, but integrating lessons to adapt next steps belongs to Act.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. Each distractor maps to a different named PDSA phase, and A alone matches the Study definition in AHRQ guidance.

cueing_check.note: All choices are parallel QI actions derived from real PDSA phases; the correct answer is not conspicuously longer and no mechanical padding was used.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: The stem places the RN as a participant in a unit quality-improvement project, matching the explicit Management of Care activity statement.
